speaker: 川畑 洸貴
title: Classification of fermionic and parafermionic CFTs in two dimensions
abstract: We investigate two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) with affine su(2) and su(3) algebra symmetry. Their bosonic modular-invariant partition functions have been fully classified based on the ADE classification. In this work, we extend the classification to include fermionic and parafermionic CFTs with the same affine symmetries, utilizing techniques of fermionization and parafermionization. We find that the fermionic and parafermionic su(2) models are related to non-simply laced Dynkin diagrams. We also discuss an alternative way of classification using 3d topological field theories.

speaker: Franz Ciceri
title: Holography for the IKKT matrix model
abstract: A particularly interesting corner of holographic dualities is the correspondence between type II strings on near-horizon Dp branes geometries and d = p+1 dimensional super Yang-Mills theories with sixteen supercharges. For the extremal case p=-1, this suggests a holographic duality for the large N limit of the IKKT matrix model. Despite intriguing and highly non-trivial results in the IKKT model, this duality has so far remained largely unexplored. In the bulk, the dual D(-1)-instanton background corresponds to a half-supersymmetric solution of Euclidean IIB supergravity with flat metric and non-trivial dilaton/axion profile. In this talk, I will explain how to construct a one-dimensional supergravity theory which describes the full non-linear dynamics of the lowest Kaluza-Klein fluctuations around the D-instanton background. This theory provides a powerful tool to study the holographic duality involving the IKKT model and its deformations. I will in particular discuss the structure of the BPS multiplet of gauge invariant operators in the IKKT model that is dual to the one-dimensional supergravity multiplet.

speaker: Kotaro Tamaoka
title: Black hole interior from pseudo entropy
abstract: We study pseudo entropy, a generalization of von Neumann (entanglement) entropy to the (reduced) transition matrix, as a holographic probe of the black hole interior. We consider two setups where the holographic screen is located at (1) the asymptotic boundary (i.e., the conventional setup in AdS/CFT) and (2) inside the black hole. For setup (1), the pseudo entropy for certain subsystems corresponds to the so-called timelike entanglement. We propose that timelike entanglement serves as a direct probe of the black hole singularity. For setup (2), we observe that the pseudo entropy can significantly exceed the black hole entropy in general dimensions. We discuss possible connections to the non-isometric nature of the black hole interior, tensor networks, and $T\overline{T}$-deformation.

speaker: Hirotaka Hayashi
title: 6d/5d gauge theories from web diagrams
abstract: 5-brane web diagrams are a powerful tool to study 5d theories and also 6d theories compactified on a circle. Gluing three or four 5-brane web diagrams may yield a new type of web diagrams which are expected to describe a larger class of 6d/5d theories. In this talk, we construct web diagrams with trivalent or quadrivalent gluing which describe 5d theories obtained from circle compactifications of 6d gauge theories with exceptional gauge groups. We also propose web diagrams with trivalent gluing which describe 5d theories associated with 6d SO(12) gauge theories with spinor matter. A nice feature of the web diagrams is that it is possible to compute the partition functions of the 5d theories described by the web diagrams by using the topological vertex formalism.

speaker: Jan Albert
title: Pushing the S-matrix bootstrap
abstract: First introduced in the 60s, positivity bounds for S-matrices have undergone a revival in the past few years, with systematic implementations that improve by the day. Among the recent results are sharp bounds on the EFTs of various gauge and gravitational theories. A common feature of the resulting exclusion regions, however, is that they tend to be saturated by S-matrices that are physically not that interesting. In this talk, I will discuss what assumptions can take us beyond this paradigm. After a brief recap on the subject, I will describe how positivity bounds define a bootstrap problem closely analogous to the well-known conformal bootstrap. This analogy will motivate new assumptions, which we will then apply to large N confining gauge theories and to weakly-coupled completions of 10d supergravity. I will explain how this refinement leads to peculiar solutions which are, respectively, surprisingly close to real-world QCD and tree-level string theory.

speaker: Takashi Toma
title: Probing pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone dark matter evading direct detection bounds
abstract: Dark matter direct detection experiments impose strong constraints on thermal dark matter models. If one still believes in thermal dark matter scenarios, a mechanism that naturally evades these strong constraints is required. Pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone dark matter is one such candidate because its scattering amplitude with a nucleon is highly suppressed by momentum transfer in the non-relativistic regime. Starting from the simplest model, we explore further extensions that address certain theoretical shortcomings of the basic framework. Additionally, we highlight a potential signature of pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone dark matter that could be observed if it is boosted by mechanisms such as semi-annihilations or self-annihilations of additional heavy stable particles.

speaker: Ippo Orii
title: On dimensions of (2+1)D abelian bosonic topological systems on unoriented manifolds
abstract: Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) is a type of Quantum Field Theory (QFT) that is independent of the metric of the spacetime manifold. One interesting aspect of TQFT is that it is rigorously defined by Atiyah's axioms. However, it is not well understood how to handle cases where the spacetime manifold is unoriented, since Atiyah's axioms assume the orientability of spacetime. In this talk, I will discuss one of the main results of [arxiv:2502.13532], where we proved that, for any unoriented surface, we can assign Hilbert spaces compatibly in abelian bosonic systems.

speaker: Hidenori Sonoda
title: The effective potential of a Yukawa model in the large $N$ with or without a cutoff
abstract: The effective potential of the $\mathbf{Z}_2$ invariant Yukawa model is calculated in the limit of a large number of fermions with a UV cutoff $\Lambda$. There is an upper limit to $\Lambda$ beyond which the effective potential is unstable. Though the result may be known to many in the audience, allow me to share what I have learned from a simple calculation.

speaker: Yuya Kusuki
title: 【Journal Club】

speaker: Hidenori Fukaya
title: K-theoretic computation of the Atiyah(-Patodi)-Singer index of lattice Dirac operators
abstract: We show that the Wilson Dirac operator in lattice gauge theory can be identified as a mathematical object in K-theory and that its associated spectral flow is equal to the index. In comparison to the standard lattice Dirac operator index, our formulation does not require the Ginsparg-Wilson relation and has broader applicability to systems with boundaries and to the mod-two version of the indices in general dimensions. We numerically verify that the K and KO group formulas reproduce the known index theorems in continuum theory. We examine the Atiyah-Singer index on a flat two-dimensional torus and, for the first time, demonstrate that the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer index with nontrivial curved boundaries, as well as the mod-two versions, can be computed on a lattice.

speaker: Seishi Enomoto
title: Explosive production of Higgs particles and implications for heavy dark matter
abstract: In this talk, we propose a new Higgs-portal dark matter scenario considering the Higgsplosion effect, which is a hypothesis of the significant production rate of high multiplicity of Higgs particles at high $\sqrt{s}$. Our scenario allows heavy Higgs-portal dark matter of $m_\chi\gtrsim{\cal O}(1)$~TeV, while the typical scenario indicates the order of ${\cal O}(10-100)$~GeV. We show that the multiplicity can be as large as ${\cal O}(200)$ for the parameters of the Standard Model Higgs, independently of the kinematics of the particle production process. Our result is applicable to a wider class of models with other scalar fields, opening a new window for heavy DM.

speaker: Masahiro Hoshino
title: Quantum resources in critical quantum spin chains
abstract:
This seminar explores the universal behavior of quantum resources in many-body systems through the lens of conformal field theory (CFT). The first part is devoted to entanglement—a fundamental resource for quantum communication. While entanglement properties are well-characterized in equilibrium, we investigate its behavior in non-equilibrium systems. We demonstrate how boundary CFT describes critical states under measurement and decoherence processes, with particular focus on entanglement swapping: the generation of entanglement solely through Bell-state measurements [1]. The second part addresses nonstabilizerness (quantum magic), an increasingly recognized essential resource for universal quantum computation. We introduce the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) as a computationally tractable measure of nonstabilizerness and explain recent numerical observations of its universal behavior in critical quantum spin chains. Our recent work reveals the origin of this universality through boundary CFT calculations of the SRE, establishing a field-theoretical framework that illuminates the universal behaviors of nonstabilizerness in quantum many-body systems [2].

[1] M. Hoshino, M. Oshikawa, Y. Ashida, arXiv:2406.12377

[2] M. Hoshino, M. Oshikawa, Y. Ashida, arXiv:2503.13599

speaker: Yuefeng Liu
title: 【Journal Club】

speaker: Hiromasa Watanabe
title: Lattice gradient flows (de-)stabilizing topological sectors and an application
abstract: We investigate the stability of the topological charge under gradient flow, taking the admissibility condition into account. For SU(2) lattice gauge theory with the Wilson action at $\beta = 2.45$ on a $12^4$ lattice, we numerically demonstrate that gradient flows with the Iwasaki and DBW2 gauge actions significantly stabilize the topological sectors. These flows exhibit qualitatively different behavior compared to those with the Wilson and tree-level Symanzik actions. This behavior is closely related to the stability of the one-instanton configuration, which depends on the choice of the flow action. Furthermore, our results suggest a rapid convergence of the topological charge in lattice simulations, which is advantageous in various applications. One such example is the computation of the ’t Hooft loop on the lattice, which will be discussed if time permits.

speaker: Jaydeep Kumar Basak
title: A New Measure of Genuine Multipartite Entanglement
abstract: In this talk, I will introduce ``Latent entropy" (L-entropy) as a novel measure to characterize genuine multipartite entanglement in pure states, applicable to quantum systems with both finite and infinite degrees of freedom. This measure, derived from an upper bound on reflected entropy, attains its maximum for three-party GHZ states and $n=4,5$-party $2$-uniform states. I will also show the generalization of this measure for higher party states. Furthermore, I will discuss an analogue of the Page curve in multiboundary wormholes. If time permits, I will show the behaviour of multipartite entanglement in random states.

speaker: Hiroyasu Tajima
title: Recent Progress in the Resource Theory of Asymmetry
abstract:
Symmetry is now one of the most important guiding principles in modern physics. In recent years, the resource theory of asymmetry (RTA) has been actively explored as a framework for understanding the role of symmetry from a resource-theoretic perspective. Despite its promise, the impact of RTA has long been limited by several unresolved foundational issues. Chief among them is the absence—except for the groups U(1) [1-3] and Z_2 [1]—of a complete measure, a resource monotone that fully characterises i.i.d. state transformations. Just as entanglement entropy plays a central role in entanglement theory, identifying the complete measure is a primary goal in any resource theory.

Very recently, this problem has been solved for all compact Lie groups [4] and for all finite groups [5]. Furthermore, the more demanding non-i.i.d. conversion problem has been settled for the U(1) case [6]. In this talk, I will survey these advances, beginning with the foundations of resource theories. I will also discuss several applications of the RTA, focusing on unified constraints that span multiple areas of physics imposed by RTA [7-9].

speaker: Shutaro Shimamura
title: Foliated-exotic duality in fractonic QFTs
abstract: Fractonic quantum field theory (QFT) is a non-relativistic QFT characterized by subsystem symmetry, a type of generalized global symmetry. Two continuum descriptions of fractonic QFT have been proposed: exotic (tensor gauge) QFT and foliated QFT. We find exact correspondences between the tensor gauge fields in exotic QFT and the foliated gauge fields in foliated QFT, and we establish an example of duality between these two types of fractonic QFTs. We refer to this as the foliated-exotic duality. This duality provides a powerful tool for analyzing fractonic QFTs. By combining it with the anomaly inflow mechanism for subsystem symmetry, we can construct previously unknown foliated descriptions of fractonic QFTs that are equivalent to the known exotic QFTs.

speaker: Coh Miyao
title: 【Journal Club】

speaker: Nagare Katayama
title: 2d Cardy-Rabinovici model with the modified Villain lattice: Exact dualities and symmetries
abstract: The Cardy-Rabinovici model is a toy model of the lattice U(1) gauge theories to study various oblique confinement states associated with the nonzero θ angles. We reformulate the 2d version of this model using the modified Villain lattice formalism, and we establish the exact θ periodicity for the Witten effect and the strong-weak duality at the finite lattice spacings. We then study the phase structure of this model based on the duality, symmetry and anomaly, and the perturbative renormalization group.

speaker: Mariko Kikuchi
title: Process renormalization scheme of two Higgs doublet models for future precision measurements
abstract:
Precise theoretical predictions for Higgs observables are essential, especially considering upcoming precision measurements at the HL-LHC and future lepton colliders.
In extended Higgs models such as Two Higgs Doublet Models (2HDMs), radiative corrections must be carefully handled when evaluating deviations from Standard Model (SM) predictions.
The properties of the 125 GeV Higgs boson (h) are modified at tree level by Higgs mixing, with the mixing angle characterizing the “alignmentness” of the Higgs sector.
However, the conventional definition of alignment via mixing angles becomes ambiguous due to radiative corrections.
We propose a renormalization scheme where “alignmentness” is defined through physical observables, using the processes h→Zττ and h→ττ to determine counterterms.
In this scheme, deviations in the Higgs decay rates can be consistently described by mixing parameters even at next-to-leading order (NLO).
We also compare our scheme with the conventional one and show that the results calculated by the new scheme are more closely aligned with tree-level expectations.
This talk is based on the paper [arXiv:2411.18859 [hep-ph]].

speaker: 諸井 健夫
title: 【教室談話会】量子センサーを用いた暗黒物質探査
abstract: 暗黒物質の存在は、様々な天文観測によりほぼ確実視されていますが、その直接検出にはいまだ成功していません。このため、世界中で暗黒物質の直接検出を目指した多くの実験が進められています。本談話会では、近年、量子コンピュータの開発を通じて急速に発展してきた量子技術を、暗黒物質探査へ応用する最先端の取り組みを紹介します。特に、暗黒光子やアクシオンなどの「波動的」暗黒物質に焦点を当て、各種量子センサーがそれらの検出にどのように役立つかを解説します。また、最近始動した超伝導量子ビットを用いた暗黒物質探査実験についても触れる予定です。

speaker: Shu-Yu Ho
title: Supernova axion emissivity with Δ(1232) resonance in heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory
abstract: In this talk, we evaluate the energy loss rate of supernovae induced by the axion emission process π− + p → n + a with the Δ(1232) resonance in the heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory for the first time. Given the axion-nucleon-∆ interactions, we include the previously ignored Δ-mediated graphs to the π− + p → n + a process. In particular, the Δ_0-mediated diagram can give a resonance contribution to the supernova axion emission rate when the center-of-mass energy of the pion and proton approaches the Δ(1232) mass. With these new contributions, we find that for the typical supernova temperatures, compared with the earlier work with the axion-nucleon (and axion-pion-nucleon contact) interactions, the supernova axion emissivity can be enhanced by a factor of ∼ 4(2) in the Kim-Shifman-Vainshtein-Zakharov model and up to a factor of ∼ 5(2) in the Dine-Fischler-Srednicki-Zhitnitsky model with small tanβ values. Remarkably, we notice that the Δ(1232) resonance gives a destructive contribution to the supernova axion emission rate at high supernova temperatures, which is a nontrivial result in this study.

title: Subdimensional Particles and Geometry-Dependent Symmetries
abstract:
Recently, subdimensional particles, including fractons, have attracted much attention across different areas of physics.
In this talk, I will present a new field-theoretic realization of subdimensional particles that carefully incorporates the underlying foliation structure.
The resulting theory exhibits novel types of symmetries that are tightly tied to the background geometry, and shows several striking features compared to conventional field theories.
This talk is based on arXiv:2408.05048 (with H. Ebisu, M. Honda, and S. Shimamori) as well as ongoing works.

speaker: Vyacheslav S. Rychkov
title: About analytic continuation of quantum field theories in non-integer dimensions
abstract: Analytic continuation in dimension has been used first as a way to regularize perturbative quantum field theory. But since the work of Wilson and Fisher, quantum field theory in d-dimension has been used more radically, to connect theories living say, in d=4, to theories in d=3 and d=2. Mathematically it's not fully clear what this means. I will give some thoughts about this subject, and I will describe some recent paradoxes which arise when one consider expansion of O(N) models around d=2, based on recent work with Fabiana De Cesare.

speaker: Tatsuya Yamaoka
title: Non-singlet conserved charges and anomalies in 3+1D staggered fermions
abstract:
We study a $(3+1)$-dimensional staggered fermion Hamiltonian system with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
In addition to the conventional vector $\mathrm{U}(1)_V$ symmetry generated by $Q_0$, we identify a set of new conserved charges $Q_i$ $(i = x,y,z)$.
These charges satisfy the Onsager algebra and represent previously unnoticed exact symmetries of the lattice Hamiltonian.
We show that, in the continuum limit, the conserved charges $Q_i$ become generators of $\mathrm{U}(1)_{F_i}$ subgroups embedded in the chiral symmetry group $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R$.
Furthermore, we demonstrate that the charges $Q_i$ precisely encode information about the symmetry structure and quantum anomalies of the infrared quantum field theory.

speaker: Toshiki Onagi
title: Conformal Bootstrap with Duality-Inspired Fusion Rules
abstract:
Since the establishment of Conformal Field Theory (CFT) by Belavin, Polyakov, and Zamolodchikov in 1984, which successfully solved the critical 2D Ising model, CFT has developed rapidly and become an indispensable framework for understanding critical phenomena. While the axiomatic system introduced by BPZ provides a classification for 2D critical phenomena with diverse applications, higher-dimensional theories lack the integrability found in two dimensions, leaving many problems unsolved to this day.

In this context, the Conformal Bootstrap program, revitalized by Slava Rychkov and others, has played a crucial role in understanding higher-dimensional critical phenomena by constraining the parameter space based solely on the theory's self-consistency.

In this seminar, I will discuss a novel method that incorporates duality-inspired fusion rules into the bootstrap equations. As a notable application, I will address the "conformal window" problem in three-dimensional QED (QED3), a long-standing open problem. QED3 is a vital model for understanding quark confinement; not only does it resemble the chiral phase transition of QCD at small flavor numbers, but it also allows for a rigorous proof of confinement and mass gap generation via the semiclassical analysis known as the Polyakov mechanism.

speaker: Yoshiki Uchida
title: Composite Asymmetric Dark Matter from Primordial Black Holes
abstract:
We investigate a cogenesis scenario for composite asymmetric dark matter framework: a dark sector has a similar strong dynamics to quantum chromodynamics in the standard model, and the dark-sector counterpart of baryons is the dark matter candidate.
The Hawking evaporation of primordial black holes plays the role of a source of heavy scalar particles whose CP-violating decay into quarks and dark quarks provides particle--anti-particle asymmetries in baryons and dark matter, respectively.
Primordial black holes should evaporate after the electroweak phase transition and before the big-bang nucleosynthesis for explaining the baryon asymmetry of the Universe and for consistent cosmology.
We find that this scenario explains the observed values for both baryon and dark matter energy densities when the heavy scalar particles have a mass of 10^6-10^9 GeV and the primordial black holes have masses of 10^7-10^9 g.

This talk is based on arXiv:2511.16354, which is currently under review in JHEP.

speaker: Shigeki Matsumoto
title: WIMPs: Where We Stand and What Comes Next
abstract:
Dark matter is one of the most persistent mysteries in modern physics. It is central to particle physics, cosmology, and astrophysics, yet the effort to identify and detect it has grown into an intrinsically interdisciplinary enterprise that involves atomic and nuclear physics, condensed matter physics, chemistry, and precision measurement. Although its gravitational imprint is firmly established, the microscopic nature of dark matter remains unknown. Remarkably, even its characteristic mass scale is largely unconstrained, spanning an enormous range from ultralight wave-like candidates around $10^{-22}\,\mathrm{eV}$ to macroscopic compact objects up to $\sim 10^{35}\,\mathrm{g}$. This breadth has motivated a diverse set of theoretical proposals and search strategies across many energy, length, and time scales.

In this seminar, I will first give a structured overview of the dark matter problem, emphasizing how different mass regimes map onto distinct physical pictures and experimental approaches. I will then focus on a particularly well motivated framework, thermal dark matter, often discussed in connection with WIMPs. Thermal dark matter is defined by the assumption that the dark sector was once in thermal equilibrium with the Standard Model in the early Universe, and that the present day relic abundance was set dynamically through freeze out or closely related mechanisms. This paradigm is compelling because it ties the dark matter density to microphysics rather than initial conditions, is embedded in the successful thermal history of standard cosmology, and connects early Universe interactions to concrete experimental signatures today. Thermal candidates also arise naturally in broad classes of beyond the Standard Model theories, including supersymmetry, grand unification, and hidden sector constructions.

Finally, I will summarize the current landscape of theoretical developments and the status of searches, from collider and intensity frontier probes to direct detection, indirect searches, and cosmological and astrophysical constraints. The goal is to provide a systematic and intuitive picture of where the leading opportunities and challenges lie across mass scales, and what near and mid term prospects may be most promising.

speaker: Motoko Fujiwara
title: Soft Collinear Effective Theory for heavy dark matter annihilation: spin-0, 1/2, and 1
abstract: Electroweakly interacting stable particles in the ${\cal O} (1-10)$ TeV mass range are well-motivated dark matter candidates with strong experimental prospects. Gamma-ray line-like features are expected to provide a smoking-gun signature for indirect detection and will be probed by future gamma-ray observations. However, a large mass hierarchy between heavy dark matter and electroweak mediators introduces theoretical complexities due to non-perturbative effects, making precise predictions challenging. In this talk, we review Effective Field Theory approaches to control such uncertainties and discuss the spin dependence of dark matter in the gamma-ray spectrum.

speaker: Shohei Okawa
title: Minimal Flavor Violation and Dark Matter
abstract:
Minimal Flavor Violation (MFV) offers a compelling framework for exploring physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). It postulates that the approximate U(3)^5 flavor symmetry in the Standard Model is also respected by BSM physics, with breaking controlled solely by quark and lepton Yukawa matrices. Within the MFV, any new physics sector predicts the same hierarchical patterns of flavor-violating observables as the Standard Model.
Interestingly, MFV can also ensure the stability of the lightest of new QCD-singlet fields transforming nontrivially under the U(3)^5 flavor group, without introducing any ad hoc symmetry. Such a new flavored field can thus serve as a good dark matter candidate, provided it is electrically neutral. In this seminar, I will first review the basic idea of the MFV hypothesis and its implication for the stability of new flavored fields. I will then show that lifetimes of heavy flavor components can be much longer than the age of the Universe, thereby allowing these particles to act as decaying dark matter candidates. Lastly, I will discuss several phenomenological aspects of this multi-component dark matter scenario and comment on possible generalizations to the lepton sector and to broader symmetry structures.

speaker: Daniele Dorigoni
title: Modular Structures in N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory
abstract: In this talk I present recent results in the study of exact correlation functions of half-BPS operators in N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory (SYM) averaged over the space-time insertion points. I review how these integrated correlation functions can be obtained from a matrix model formulation of the N=4 path-integral and then move to present two different integrated correlation functions of four superconformal primary operators of the stress-tensor multiplet, holographically related to scattering amplitudes of 4-gravitons in type IIB superstring theory on an AdS_5 x S^5 background. A key player in this discussion is electro-magnetic duality of N=4 SYM which provides strong constraints on the coupling dependence of such observables. Lastly, I discuss an N=4 SYM integrated correlation function of two superconformal primary operators in the stress tensor multiplet in the presence of a half-BPS line defect operator, such as a Wilson line. Electro-magnetic duality is again fundamental in understanding the exact dependence from the complexified Yang-Mills coupling and the modular properties of such observables.

speaker: Takamasa Ando
title: Symmetry Spans and Enforced Gaplessness
abstract:
Anomaly matching is a powerful tool for constraining possible infrared behavior using only the global symmetries of UV theories. For example, general anomalies for finite symmetries exclude the possibility of a unique gapped ground state. In this talk, I will explain another mechanism for constraining possible IR theories, based on a “symmetry span,” which is a pair of symmetries sharing a nontrivial subsymmetry.
Using general constraints imposed by symmetry spans on possible gapped theories, I will provide an application to enforced gaplessness, a phenomenon that forbids any relativistic gapped theory in the infrared. The mechanism introduced here can operate even for UV theories with only discrete symmetries and non-anomalous continuous symmetries, both of which admit well-understood lattice realizations.
In the talk, I will explain both continuum CFTs and lattice models that realize this enforced gaplessness.

abstract: 保存則、相転移、素粒子の分類など、対称性は理論物理学のさまざまな場面で私たちの理解を導いてきました。近年、その概念は「一般化対称性」へと拡張され、特に変換が群をなさない「圏論的対称性」が注目されています。圏論的対称性は量子力学特有の対称性であり、物性論から高エネルギー物理まで幅広い問題に新しい視点を与えます。本講演では、その基本的な考え方を紹介し、いくつかの応用について概観します。

speaker: Yuta Hamada
title: 6d Supergravity Blocks
abstract: We propose a systematic framework for constructing six-dimensional supergravity theories with eight supercharges that respect all known consistency constraints, including anomaly cancellation and the non-perturbative H-string constraints. The basic objects in this framework are supergravity blocks, which are minimal collections of tensor multiplets consisting of a single little string theory. Any consistent 6d N=(1,0) supergravity theory can then be obtained by gluing compatible blocks and subsequently enhancing the gauge algebras and matter content. As a first step toward establishing this framework concretely, we provide a complete classification of the non-Higgsable supergravity blocks, namely those built from tensor multiplets that support only non-Higgsable gauge algebras.

speaker: Keita Tsuji
title: What happens to wavepackets of fermions when scattered by the Maldacena-Ludwig wall?
abstract:
In four-dimensional QED, the scattering of a fermion off a monopole leads to the Callan-Rubakov problem: the incoming elementary fermion turns into an exotic excitation with fractional quantum numbers. In the s-wave approximation, this problem reduces to a two-dimensional boundary CFT. In the four-flavor case, the monopole boundary condition can be described, after unfolding, by a non-invertible defect known as the Maldacena-Ludwig wall.
In this talk, I will discuss the results of [arXiv:2603.25508], in which we obtained an explicit expression for the outgoing state of a fermion-antifermion pair scattered off the Maldacena-Ludwig wall. We showed that the energy density and charge density remain localized and carry the expected fractional charge, while the expectation value of the number of original fermions diverges in the sharply localized limit.

speaker: Sunjin Choi
title: Holography with ADE singularities
abstract: I will talk about aspects of the AdS/CFT correspondence for N=4 U(N) super Yang-Mills theory on S^3/\Gamma, where \Gamma is a finite subgroup of SU(2) leading to an ADE singularity in the bulk AdS geometry. I will show that a large vacuum degeneracy arises from the choice of gauge holonomy on S^3/\Gamma. On the gravity side, I will argue that the bulk ADE singularity supports topological degrees of freedom responsible for this degeneracy, which admit an effective description in terms of a 3d level-N Chern-Simons theory, whose gauge group is determined by \Gamma. Finally, I will comment on how the one-form symmetries of the N=4 super Yang-Mills theory are realized on the Chern-Simons theory side.

title: Revisiting neutrino oscillations in vacuum with wave packets
abstract: Neutrino oscillations have attracted considerable interest both experimentally and theoretically, and have been the subject of vigorous research for many years. One theoretically sound derivation of neutrino oscillations (in vacuum) is to describe them as wave-packet transitions. However, conventional derivations have relied on several presumptions, such as the use of asymptotic forms of the wave-packet profile. In this talk, we will discuss how a generalised formula can be derived to describe a wider range of situations, in which certain presumptions are relaxed, specifically focusing on the Gaussian wave packet state.

speaker: Rajath Radhakrishnan
title: Non-invertible symmetries of higher-dimensional QFTs act (almost) invertibly on local operators
abstract:
Symmetries of a quantum field theory are implemented by topological operators. These are special extended operators whose correlation functions are insensitive to continuous deformations of their support. The classification of generalized symmetries thus reduces to understanding the spectrum of such topological operators across different codimensions.

While a generic QFT may admit infinitely many topological operators, their topological nature imposes strong consistency conditions on their structure. In this talk, I will present a set of such constraints in 2+1 and 3+1 dimensions and highlight how they severely restrict the spectrum of topological operators in higher dimensions, in contrast to 1+1 dimensions. Using these constraints, I will argue that the action of non-invertible symmetries on local operators in higher dimensions is highly restricted. In particular, this action is either invertible or, or can be rendered invertible by gauging an appropriate higher-form symmetry. This talk is based on the paper arXiv: 2603.03438 with Pavel Putrov.

speaker: Ryohei Kobayashi
title: Remarks on invertible phases with non-onsite symmetry
abstract: We consider invertible phases protected by non-onsite symmetries carrying nontrivial lattice anomaly indices. While lattice anomalies are usually viewed as obstructions to symmetric short-range-entangled (SRE) states, we show that anomalous lattice symmetries can nevertheless admit invertible phases that are not SRE, and can moreover shift the set of symmetry-compatible invertible phases. In particular, we consider a fermionic Z4F symmetry, symmetric invertible phases have integer chiral central charge, whereas a non-onsite symmetry with nontrivial lattice anomaly index obstructs all such phases despite having trivial continuum 't Hooft anomaly. We resolve this by constructing an exact exponentially quasi-local Z4F symmetry of a p+ip superconductor with c- = 1/2. We compute its lattice anomaly, and find that the symmetry indeed forbids integer c- invertible states. The allowed invertible phases are consequently shifted to c- in Z + 1/2. By gauging the fermion parity of the p+ip superconductor, one obtains an Ising topological order enriched by a Z4 symmetry. We describe the corresponding symmetry structure in terms of a fusion 2-category. We further show that the p+ip state admits an enlarged non-onsite U(1)f symmetry, providing an analogue of fractional quantum Hall response in an invertible phase. This non-onsite U(1)f symmetry again forbids Chern insulators carrying integer c-, while being compatible with invertible states with c- in Z+1/2. This result motivates a systematic study of new classes of invertible phases and spin liquids enriched by non-onsite symmetries. The talk will be based on recent works 2609.12042, 2608.12455.

speaker: Javier Moreno
title: de Sitter holography from a Lorentzian torus
abstract: We show that the quantum entanglement between the conformal field theories (CFTs) living on the future and past boundaries in the de Sitter/conformal field theory (dS/CFT) correspondence can be described by Wick rotating to a geometry with two timelike directions. We propose a new realization of the dS/CFT correspondence in which quantum gravity on this two-time geometry is holographically dual to a CFT defined on a Lorentzian torus. We show that this duality reproduces key features of dS holography, including the dS entropy, correlation functions, and pseudoentropy. Finally, by extending the framework of path-integral optimization, we explain how dS spacetime emerges from the CFT on the Lorentzian torus.

title: A particle on a ring or: how I learned to stop worrying and love theta-vacua
abstract: Although the QCD Lagrangian allows CP violation by the theta-term, no such effect has been observed yet. This puzzle is called the strong CP problem. In this talk, I will review a recent debate on the order of limit in the path integral formulation of strong CP violation, and discuss the validity of the formulation by focusing on quantum mechanics on a circle.

abstract:
The resource theory of asymmetry provides a systematic framework for quantifying symmetry breaking. After a brief introduction to the resource theory of asymmetry, I will
discuss its applications in many-body physics. I will emphasize how the resource-theoretic viewpoint determines which measures of asymmetry are physically reliable, and discuss how different monotones capture distinct aspects of symmetry breaking.

speaker: Okuto Morikawa (森川 億人)
title: Center-Twisted Gribov Spectra and the Question of Confinement
abstract: Color confinement in Yang–Mills theory has been studied from several viewpoints, including the Gribov–Zwanziger scenario and center symmetry. In this talk, I will investigate their possible connection using the twisted partition function associated with the electric $\mathbb{Z}_N^{[1]}$ 1-form symmetry.On a finite torus with a nontrivial ’t Hooft twist, I will discuss how the twist modifies the Faddeev–Popov spectrum and study the resulting finite-volume response in the refined Gribov–Zwanziger framework. The analysis also clarifies what is still missing for a direct connection to a center-symmetry criterion for confinement.
